examples.en: My friend nodded at what I said.
The teacher smiled and nodded.
I'm sleepy, so my head keeps nodding.

examples.ko: 고개를 끄덕거리며 이야기를 듣는 모습이 좋아요.
examples.en: I like how you listen to the story while nodding.
The child nods his head as if to say he understands.

examples.ko: 다들 고개를 끄덕거리지만 사실은 잘 모르는 것 같아요.
examples.en: Everyone is nodding, but they seem not to really understand.

explain: '끄덕이다'와 뜻이 거의 같지만 '-거리다'가 붙어서 고개를 여러 번 반복해서 움직이는 느낌이 있어요. 한 번 끄덕이는 동작은 '끄덕이다'가 자연스럽고, 보통 '고개를 끄덕거리다'처럼 써요.

phrases.en: He nodded without saying a word.
phrases.nuance_ko: '끄덕거리다'보다 한두 번 가볍게 끄덕이는 느낌이라 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Feels like one or two light nods, and is more common than '끄덕거리다'.

phrases.en: They listened to me, nodding their head.
phrases.nuance_ko: 듣는 동안 계속 고개를 움직일 때 '-며'로 이어서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use '-며' for nodding repeatedly while listening.

phrases.en: The child nodded again and again while listening to the story.
phrases.nuance_ko: 고개를 여러 번 끄덕이는 모습을 나타내는 부사예요.
phrases.nuance_en: An adverb showing repeated nodding.

explain_en: Nodding several times while listening or agreeing. It means almost the same as '끄덕이다', but the '-거리다' ending gives a feeling of repeating the movement several times. For a single nod, '끄덕이다' sounds more natural, and it is usually used as '고개를 끄덕거리다'.

examples.en: Why are you showing off so much?

examples.ko: 아무도 안 시켰는데 혼자 나대고 있어요.
examples.en: Nobody told him to, but he's busy butting in alone.
If you make a fuss over nothing, it's actually embarrassing.
My friend was showing off, and the mood got weird.
That kid tends to show off everywhere.
Don't push yourself forward so much, and stay quiet.

explain: 필요 없이 나서거나 잘난 척하며 설치는 사람에게 쓰는 부정적인 말투예요. 친구끼리 농담으로 쓰기도 하지만 윗사람이나 처음 만난 사람에게 쓰면 무례해요. 비슷한 말로 '설치다', '깝죽대다'가 있어요.

phrases.example: 친구가 나한테 "시키지 않은 일에는 나대지 마."라고 했어요.
phrases.en: My friend told me, "Don't butt in on things nobody asked you to do."
phrases.nuance_ko: '나대다'를 반말 금지 표현으로 쓴 말이에요. 아주 친한 사이에서만 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A casual command form of 나대다 meaning 'don't show off or butt in'. Use it only with very close friends.

phrases.example: 회의 때 나대는 사람은 별로 좋아 보이지 않아요.
phrases.en: People who show off at meetings don't look good.
phrases.nuance_ko: '나대다'를 사람 앞에 붙여 쓰는 활용형이에요. 그 사람을 흉볼 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A modifier form placed before a noun. It is used to criticize someone who oversteps.

phrases.en: Why are you running around making a fuss all by yourself?
phrases.nuance_ko: '나대다'와 뜻이 비슷하지만 조금 덜 거칠어서 말하기 편해요. 그래도 윗사람에게는 쓰지 않아요.
phrases.nuance_en: Close in meaning to 나대다 but slightly less harsh. Still avoid it with superiors.
phrases.en_equiv: to make a fuss; to run amok

explain_en: A negative word for someone who pushes themselves forward or acts smug when it isn't needed. Friends may use it as a joke, but it is rude to elders or people you've just met. Similar words are 설치다 and 깝죽대다.

examples.en: When class ended, the students scattered in all directions.

examples.ko: 형편이 어려워서 가족들이 뿔뿔이 흩어져 살았대요.
examples.en: I heard the family was so badly off that they lived scattered apart.

examples.ko: 비가 오자 사람들이 뿔뿔이 집으로 돌아갔어요.
examples.en: When it started raining, people went their separate ways home.

examples.ko: 졸업하면 친구들이 뿔뿔이 다른 도시로 가요.
examples.en: After graduation, friends scatter off to different cities.
After the gathering ended, we split up and went our own ways.
The startled chickens ran off in every direction.

explain: 한곳에 있던 사람이나 동물이 각자 다른 방향으로 갈라질 때 써요. '흩어지다, 헤어지다, 도망가다' 같은 말과 자주 함께 나와요.

phrases.en: When the bell rang, the children scattered in all directions.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가장 흔한 짝말로, 각자 다른 쪽으로 퍼지는 모습이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing, showing people spreading in different directions.

phrases.en: After graduation, my friends went their separate ways.
phrases.nuance_ko: 함께 있던 사람들이 각자의 길로 떠날 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when people who were together part ways.

phrases.en: The startled sparrows fled in all directions.
phrases.nuance_ko: 놀라서 사방으로 달아나는 모습에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes fleeing in every direction out of fright.

explain_en: It is used when people or animals that were together split off in different directions. It often appears with words like '흩어지다' (scatter), '헤어지다' (part) and '도망가다' (run away).

en: to be brusque; to be distant; to be icy

examples.en: That employee is a bit cold toward customers.
I'm sorry I answered so coldly.
His icy expression scared me at first.
She looks aloof, but she's actually very warm.
She turned away coldly and left.

examples.ko: 쌀쌀맞던 옆집 아저씨가 요즘은 먼저 인사해요.
examples.en: The neighbor who used to be so cold now greets me first.

explain: '쌀쌀하다'는 날씨에도 쓰지만 '쌀쌀맞다'는 사람의 태도나 말투에만 써요. 정이 없고 차갑게 대한다는 느낌이라 '냉정하다', '차갑다'와 비슷하지만 더 일상적인 말이에요.

phrases.en: I get misunderstood because of my cold way of speaking.
phrases.nuance_ko: '쌀쌀맞다'를 명사 앞에 붙인 모양이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The form placed before a noun.

phrases.en: He looks cold but is actually kind.
phrases.nuance_ko: 인상이 차갑게 보인다고 할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone gives a cold impression.

phrases.en: That teacher isn't cold, but warm.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부정형으로 차갑지 않다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form saying someone isn't cold.

explain_en: '쌀쌀하다' can describe weather, but '쌀쌀맞다' is only used for a person's attitude or tone. It means cold and unfriendly, similar to '냉정하다' or '차갑다' but more everyday.

en: to be shrewd; to be smart; to be slick

examples.ko: 그 사람은 약아빠져서 자기 이익만 챙겨요.
examples.en: He is a sly operator who only looks out for his own interests.
Be careful not to be fooled by a crafty merchant.
I can't believe how cunning this little kid is.
He acted so calculating that his friends gradually drifted away.

examples.ko: 다들 약아빠졌다고 하지만 저한테는 늘 잘해 줘요.
examples.en: Everyone says he's sly, but he's always good to me.

examples.ko: 약아빠지지 않고 정직하게 사는 게 마음 편해요.
examples.en: Living honestly without being sly gives me peace of mind.

explain: '약삭빠르다'보다 거칠고 더 나쁘게 흉보는 말투예요. 자기 이익만 챙기는 약은 사람이나 행동을 말하고, 구어에서 많이 써요. 윗사람이나 격식 있는 자리에서는 쓰지 않는 게 좋아요.

phrases.example: 그 사람은 약아빠진 사람이라 믿기 어려워요.
phrases.en: He is a crafty person, so he's hard to trust.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자기 이익만 챙기는 사람을 거칠게 흉볼 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to roughly criticize someone who only looks after their own interest.

phrases.en: That merchant is really crafty.
phrases.nuance_ko: 해요체로 말하면 구어에서 강하게 흉보는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: In 해요체, it sounds like strong criticism in casual speech.

phrases.en: Don't pull crafty tricks.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자기만 이득을 보려는 행동을 나쁘게 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to disparage self-serving actions.

explain_en: Spoken, strongly negative, too clever in a selfish way. It is a rougher and more negative way to criticize than '약삭빠르다'. It describes a person or action that is crafty and only looks after its own benefit, and it is mostly spoken. It is best avoided with superiors or in formal settings.

t90.ax: I can't believe how cunning this little kid is.

examples.en: Going back on your word like that, you're someone who says one thing and does another.
When a politician goes back on their word, they lose people's trust.

examples.ko: 그는 약속해 놓고 일구이언해서 모두가 실망했어요.
examples.en: He made a promise and then went back on it, so everyone was disappointed.

examples.ko: 어제는 된다고 했다가 오늘은 안 된다니 일구이언 아니에요?
examples.en: You said yes yesterday and no today. Isn't that going back on your word?

examples.ko: 일구이언이라는 말을 들을까 봐 신중하게 대답했어요.
examples.en: I answered carefully so I wouldn't be called two-faced.

examples.ko: 일구이언하지 않는 사람이 결국 신뢰를 얻어요.
examples.en: People who don't go back on their word end up earning trust.

explain: '일구이언(을) 하다'나 '일구이언하다'로 써요. '말을 바꾸다'와 달리 신뢰를 어겼다는 비판이 강해서 가볍게 쓰면 꽤 센 말이 돼요.

phrases.example: 그 사람은 약속을 자꾸 바꿔서 일구이언한다고 해요.
phrases.en: They say he is double-tongued because he keeps changing his promises.
phrases.nuance_ko: 동사처럼 붙여서 쓰면 말을 바꾸는 사람을 바로 비판하는 말이 돼요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used as a verb, it directly criticizes someone who goes back on their word.
phrases.en_equiv: to go back on one's word

phrases.en: If you made a promise, don't go back on your word.
phrases.nuance_ko: 상대에게 말을 바꾸지 말라고 강하게 요구할 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A strong request telling someone not to change their word.
phrases.en_equiv: don't go back on your word

phrases.en: I don't want to work with someone who says one thing and does another.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람을 꾸밀 때 쓰는 꼴로, 꽤 센 비난이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: This form describes a person and is a fairly harsh criticism.

explain_en: It is used as '일구이언(을) 하다' or '일구이언하다'. Unlike '말을 바꾸다' (to change one's words), it carries strong criticism for breaking trust, so using it casually sounds quite harsh.

examples.ko: 이 웹툰의 창작자는 아직 스무 살이에요.
examples.en: The creator of this webtoon is still twenty years old.

examples.ko: 창작자와 직접 이야기할 수 있는 행사가 있어요.
examples.en: There is an event where you can talk directly with the creator.

examples.ko: 저는 어릴 때부터 창작자가 되고 싶었어요.
examples.en: I have wanted to become a creator since I was little.

examples.ko: 좋은 창작자는 매일 조금씩 작품을 만들어요.
examples.en: A good creator makes a little work every day.

examples.ko: 창작자의 허락 없이 그림을 쓰면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You must not use a drawing without the creator's permission.
There are so many young creators on the internet.

explain: 창작자는 만든 사람 중에서도 처음부터 새로 만든 사람을 가리켜요. 그림, 노래, 글처럼 작품을 만드는 사람에게 쓰고, 공장에서 물건을 만드는 사람에게는 '제작자'나 '생산자'를 써요. 요즘은 유튜브나 웹툰에서 활동하는 사람을 말할 때 자주 들려요.

phrases.en: I want to become a webtoon creator.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 분야인지 앞에 붙여서 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put the field in front to say what kind of creator.

phrases.example: 요즘은 혼자 일하는 콘텐츠 창작자가 많아요.
phrases.en: These days there are many content creators who work alone.
phrases.nuance_ko: 영상이나 글 같은 온라인 작품을 만드는 사람에게 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: For people who make online works like videos or writing.

phrases.example: 작품을 쓰려면 창작자의 허락을 받아야 해요.
phrases.en: To use the work, you need the creator's permission.
phrases.nuance_ko: 작품을 쓸 때 권리가 누구에게 있는지 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used when talking about who holds the rights.

explain_en: Maker of art, comics, writing; the usual term for artists. 창작자 is someone who makes an original work from scratch, like a drawing, song, or story. For people who produce goods in a factory, Koreans say 제작자 or 생산자 instead. You hear it a lot now for people active on YouTube or in webtoons.

t90.ax: A good creator makes a little work every day.

examples.en: They say everyone comes empty-handed and leaves empty-handed.
My grandfather told me not to be greedy, since we come and go empty-handed.

examples.ko: 돈을 많이 모아도 공수래공수거인데 뭐 하러 싸워요?
examples.en: Even if you save lots of money you leave empty-handed, so why fight?

examples.ko: 공수래공수거라는 말이 요즘 더 마음에 와닿아요.
examples.en: The saying about coming and going empty-handed resonates with me more these days.
After going to my friend's funeral, the saying about coming and going empty-handed came to mind.

examples.ko: 공수래공수거를 알면서도 다들 더 갖고 싶어 해요.
examples.en: Even though they know we come and go empty-handed, everyone wants to have more.

explain: 욕심을 버리라고 말할 때 어른들이 자주 쓰는 사자성어예요. 보통 '공수래공수거라고 하잖아요', '공수래공수거인데'처럼 문장 속에서 인용하듯 써요. 재산이나 욕심의 허무함을 말하는 분위기라서 가벼운 농담보다는 진지한 대화에 어울려요.

phrases.en: Life is come empty, return empty, so don't be too greedy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 인생 전체를 말하며 욕심을 내려놓으라고 조언할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to advise letting go of greed, speaking of life as a whole.
phrases.en_equiv: life is come empty, go empty

phrases.en: We come and go empty-handed, so let's live comfortably.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이유를 말하는 연결형이라서 충고나 위로 앞에 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: A reason-giving connective, placed before advice or comfort.
phrases.en_equiv: since we come and go empty-handed

phrases.en: The elders say we come and go empty-handed.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어른들의 말을 인용해서 전할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to quote what elders say.
phrases.en_equiv: they say come empty, go empty

explain_en: It is a four-character saying that older people often use when telling someone to let go of greed. It is typically quoted within a sentence, as in '공수래공수거라고 하잖아요' or '공수래공수거인데'. It talks about the emptiness of wealth and desire, so it suits serious conversation more than light jokes.

en: to predict; to forecast; to prophesy

examples.ko: 옛날에는 별을 보고 날씨를 예언하려고 했어요.
examples.en: In the old days, people tried to predict the weather by looking at the stars.

examples.ko: 그는 경제가 곧 나빠질 거라고 예언하고 있어요.
examples.en: He is predicting that the economy will soon get worse.

examples.ko: 미래를 예언하는 사람은 많지만 맞히는 사람은 드물어요.
examples.en: Many people predict the future, but few get it right.

examples.ko: 책 속 마법사가 왕의 죽음을 예언해요.
examples.en: The wizard in the book foretells the king's death.

examples.ko: 아무도 그런 일이 생길 거라고 예언할 수 없었어요.
examples.en: Nobody could have predicted that such a thing would happen.

examples.ko: 누가 내일 일을 예언하면 정말 믿을 수 있겠어요?
examples.en: If someone foretold tomorrow's events, could you really believe it?

explain: 예언은 신비한 힘이나 종교적인 느낌이 있어요. 자료를 보고 미리 계산할 때는 '예측하다', 뉴스에서 앞날을 내다볼 때는 '전망하다'를 써요. 날씨나 경기 결과에는 '예언'보다 '예상'이 자연스러워요.

phrases.en: That person's prediction turned out to be right.
phrases.nuance_ko: '예언'이 사실이 되었을 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a prediction turns out to be true.

phrases.example: 옛 이야기에는 앞날을 보는 예언자가 나와요.
phrases.en: Old stories feature a prophet who sees the future.
phrases.nuance_ko: 예언하는 사람을 말하며 신비한 느낌이 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: A person who prophesies, with a mystical feel.

phrases.en: Experts forecast next year's economy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자료를 보고 미리 계산할 때는 '예언하다' 대신 이 말을 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use this instead of 예언하다 when predicting from data.

explain_en: Foretelling the future by insight or signs (별을 보고 예언하다) 예언하다 carries a mystical or religious feel. When you calculate ahead from data, use 예측하다; in news about the outlook, 전망하다. For weather or match results, 예상 is more natural than 예언.

t90.ax: The wizard in the book foretells the king's death.

examples.en: He raised his hand without hesitation.
There was no time to hesitate, so I dove right in.

examples.ko: 잠깐의 주저 끝에 그는 문을 열었어요.
examples.en: After a moment's hesitation, he opened the door.
I could sense hesitation in her voice.
Don't hesitate to ask whatever you're curious about.
I hesitated a lot before making the decision.

explain: '주저 없이', '주저하지 말고'처럼 거의 정해진 모양으로 많이 써요. 특히 '주저하지 말고 연락 주세요'는 편지나 안내문에서 정중하게 부탁할 때 자주 나와요. 말로는 '망설이지 말고'가 더 부드러워요.

phrases.example: 그는 질문을 듣고 주저 없이 대답했어요.
phrases.en: He answered without hesitation after hearing the question.
phrases.nuance_ko: 망설임 없이 바로 하는 모습을 말하는 가장 흔한 모양이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common set form for doing something right away.

phrases.example: 궁금한 게 있으면 주저하지 말고 물어보세요.
phrases.en: If you're curious about anything, don't hesitate to ask.
phrases.nuance_ko: 안내문이나 이메일에서 정중하게 부탁할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used politely in notices and emails.

phrases.en: There was no hesitation in her voice.
phrases.nuance_ko: '주저'보다 말할 때 더 부드럽고 일상적인 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A softer, more everyday word than 주저.

explain_en: It mostly appears in set patterns like 주저 없이 and 주저하지 말고. 주저하지 말고 연락 주세요 is a very common polite line in letters and notices. In speech, 망설이지 말고 sounds softer.

t90.ax: He raised his hand without hesitation.

examples.en: I have mixed feelings after hearing my friend's news.
With graduation coming up, my feelings are all mixed.
He looked out the window with a troubled expression.
I was both happy and sad, so my heart was in a tangle.

examples.ko: 이사하는 날 빈 집을 보니 착잡하더라고요.
examples.en: On moving day, seeing the empty house left me with mixed feelings.

examples.ko: 마음이 착잡해서 아무 말도 못 했어요.
examples.en: My feelings were so tangled that I couldn't say anything.

explain: 기쁨과 슬픔, 걱정이 한꺼번에 섞여 마음이 복잡하고 무거울 때 써요. '복잡하다'보다 감정이 무겁고 쓸쓸한 느낌이 더 강해요. 보통 '마음이/기분이 착잡하다'처럼 써요.

phrases.en: I came home with mixed feelings.
phrases.nuance_ko: '착잡하다'를 명사 앞에 붙여 마음 상태를 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifier form placed before a noun to describe one's state of mind.

phrases.en: For some reason my heart feels heavy and mixed today.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금의 기분을 해요체로 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The polite present form for describing how you feel now.

phrases.en: He read the letter with a conflicted look on his face.
phrases.nuance_ko: 말하지 않아도 복잡한 감정이 얼굴에 드러날 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when mixed feelings show on someone's face.

explain_en: Use it when joy, sadness and worry are mixed together and your heart feels heavy and tangled. Compared with '복잡하다', it carries a stronger sense of heaviness and loneliness. It is usually used as '마음이/기분이 착잡하다'.

en: to be expressed; to be represented; to be manifested

examples.en: That feeling is well expressed in the song.
Sadness was expressed in the painting.
This word is hard to express in English.
The season depicted in the poem is autumn.
Emotions show up on the face as they are.

examples.ko: 숫자로 표현될 수 없는 가치도 있어요.
examples.en: There are also values that can't be expressed in numbers.

explain: 감정이나 생각이 말, 그림, 얼굴 등으로 드러난다는 말이에요. '표현하다'는 내가 나타내는 것이고, '표현되다'는 감정이 주어로 나와요. 어디에 나타나는지는 '에/으로'로 말해요.

phrases.en: The sadness is well expressed in the painting.
phrases.nuance_ko: 생각이나 감정이 잘 드러난다는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Says thoughts or feelings come across well.

phrases.en: I can feel the feelings expressed in the writing.
phrases.nuance_ko: 드러난 감정이나 생각을 명사 앞에서 꾸밀 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A modifier form for a feeling or thought that has been expressed.

phrases.en: My gratitude can't be put into words.
phrases.nuance_ko: 말로 다 나타낼 수 없는 감정을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for feelings too big to put into words.

explain_en: Be expressed — in words, art or looks, general word. It means a feeling or thought shows through words, pictures or a face. '표현하다' has you expressing something, while with 표현되다 the feeling itself is the subject. '에' or '(으)로' marks where it appears.

dis.h: be expressed in words, art, or looks
gh: burst out; pent-up feelings shown outwardly

p.n: 표출되다 stresses emotion bursting outward; 표현되다 is neutral.

t90.ax: Sadness was expressed in the painting.

en: to be futile; to be empty

examples.en: I feel empty because the exam I prepared so hard for was canceled.
Feeling hollow, I just looked at the sky for a long time.
The match ended so easily that it was anticlimactic.
All the effort vanished into nothing.

examples.ko: 일이 끝나고 나니 허무하다는 생각이 들었어요.
examples.en: After the work was over, I felt a sense of emptiness.
I set small goals so I wouldn't feel empty.

explain: 열심히 했는데 결과가 없거나, 기대한 것이 갑자기 사라졌을 때의 힘 빠진 마음이에요. 비슷한 '허탈하다'는 몸에 힘이 쭉 빠지는 느낌이고, '허무하다'는 모든 것이 의미 없어진 것 같은 느낌이 더 커요. '허무하게 끝나다', '허무하게 지다'처럼 부사형으로도 많이 써요.

phrases.example: 오랫동안 준비한 일이 취소돼서 허무한 기분이 들었어요.
phrases.en: I felt empty because something I had prepared for a long time was canceled.
phrases.nuance_ko: '허무한'이 명사 '기분'을 꾸미는 쓰임으로, 감정을 설명할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifier form describing the noun 기분, used often to explain a feeling.

phrases.en: The game I was looking forward to ended anticlimactically.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기대에 비해 결과가 너무 빨리, 쉽게 끝났을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when something ends too quickly or easily compared to expectations.

phrases.example: 열심히 만든 파일이 지워져서 너무 허무했어요.
phrases.en: I felt so empty because the file I worked hard on was deleted.
phrases.nuance_ko: 과거형 해요체로, 이미 지나간 일에 힘이 빠진 마음을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The past polite form, expressing deflation over something that already happened.

explain_en: Sense of vanity after effort comes to nothing. It describes the deflated feeling when hard work leads to nothing or something you expected suddenly disappears. The similar '허탈하다' is more about strength draining out of you, while '허무하다' leans toward a feeling that everything has become meaningless. The adverb form is common too, as in '허무하게 끝나다' and '허무하게 지다'.
